messages:
ana: Quick brainstorm: propose a 'compatibility bridge' offering instead of ad-hoc pins. Goal: predictable infra cost, clear SLA, and migration lanes per customer.

mike: I like the lane idea. Lanes: fast-migrate (30d), standard (90d), extended (180d paid). Each lane defines pin TTL, support level, and traffic split rules.

chet: From infra: lanes help because we can reserve cache + index capacity per lane rather than per customer. Suggest defaults:
- fast_migrate_ttl: 30
- standard_ttl: 90
- extended_ttl: 180
- max_pinned_per_tenant: 2

dean: ML asks: require a minimal regression report for bridge enrollments: 200 sample prompts, embedding drift < 0.025, semantic pass rate > 97%. If fail, only allow temporary bridge for 14d while fix is tracked.

ana: (typo) ana: ^ meant to tag dean.

ana: product UX notes: in console, show lane selector, estimated monthly surcharge, and a one-click rollback. Add checkbox: request legal/contract amendment.

legal-bot: FYI legal prefers: "compatibility bridge" term + explicit fees in contract addendum. Auto-generated addendum template recommended.

mike: Ops constraints: set a global soft cap at 120 active bridges. Over that, auto-close new enrollments and route to waitlist. Put telemetry to alert at 80% utilization.

chet: Also add kill-switch policy: any lane with >1% user-facing errors over 1h triggers emergency rollback to previous variant.

dean: One more: add daily sampled quality dashboard for bridged traffic to spot drift early.

ana: Action items:
- Dean: publish regression report spec and dashboard sample (2d)
- Chet: infra quota + alerting spec + backfill plan (3d)
- Mike: pricing tiers + surcharge calc (3d)
- Legal-bot / legal: addendum template (2d)

mike: I'll open RW-PL-7501 and add owners. Anyone object?

chet: No objections.

dean: Fine from ML.

legal-bot: Noted. Template will be drafted.

ana: cool, closing thread. :white_check_mark:
